Definition: from ἔτης (a clansman); a comrade:--fellow, friend.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says hetaîros, it means fellow, friend. The word appears 3 times, and in Matthew it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hetaîros matters because a friend who stays is worth more than a crowd that leaves. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard; The Wedding Feast; The Arrest of Jesus in Gethsemane
